P1456 is a real, well-documented 1959-commissioned Soviet-era trunk gas pipeline (803 km, 720mm, Serpukhov [Moscow Oblast] to Leningrad/Saint Petersburg via Kalinin/Tver oblast), independently confirmed by a third-party industrial database (energybase.ru), Gazprom's own subsidiary's 50th-anniversary press release (gazprom.ru via Wayback, since the live host connect-times-out from this machine), and two independent Russian trade/regional-press retrospectives (bloknot-stavropol.ru 2025, neftianka.ru). Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both directly and consistently stated. Not a duplicate of, or misclassification against, any other row in this 28-PID roster: it is clearly distinct from the later, geographically separate Gryazovets-Leningrad pipeline family (P5534/P5535) and the Gryazovets-Vyborg lines (P0746/P5585), which run a different, more northerly corridor sourced from Vologda-region gas rather than Stavropol gas relayed via the Moscow-area Serpukhov-Moscow trunk; and distinct from Belousovo-Leningrad, a separate 1967-built pipeline that shares reconstruction contractors and combined funding with P1456 in several sources but is NOT itself a PID in this roster (no cross_row_lead needed). CAVEAT 1 (operator): Gazprom's own 2009 primary source names TWO joint operators for this line -- Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg AND Gazprom Transgaz Moscow -- consistent with the line crossing both companies' territorial zones; only Transgaz Saint Petersburg is staged as the single Operator value (see Operator [ref] researcher_notes) since it is also the entity named in a live, current (2026) maintenance tender. CAVEAT 2 (cost): the only cost figure found (~40 billion rubles, neftegaz.ru 2016) is an aggregate covering a COMBINED reconstruction program spanning both Serpukhov-Leningrad and the separate, non-roster Belousovo-Leningrad pipeline -- correctly left UNRESOLVED for SegmentCost rather than misattributed to this row alone. CAVEAT 3 (pressure): a 5.4 MPa figure appearing in 2020 reconstruction-approval press coverage is explicitly scoped to a small NEW branch spur (150mm, 3.6km, connecting a Novgorod CHP plant) built as part of the 9th reconstruction stage, not the 720mm main trunk's own rated pressure -- correctly left UNRESOLVED rather than misattributed.
